## Judges' verdicts

### Judge 1

Skeptical-practitioner verdict. The tape sets the ceiling before any model runs: 1m Foundation is +1.9 pts per trade gross against ~16 pts of cost (mean net -922 INR, 15.2% winners, 4,502 IS SETUPs in 579 active sessions); 5m is 184 IS winners with the top decile carrying ~46% of gross and an IS-to-OOS mean shift from -277 to -1,060 per trade. So any gate must find a subset whose expectancy clears ~16-20 pts, and the whole signal lives in a few hundred trades on 1m and a few dozen on 5m. On that sample the block-bootstrap CI of a kept-vs-skipped difference will be several hundred INR per trade wide; most candidates will not clear it, and that is the honest expected outcome. Every library the 18 studies name is present (sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib) and statsmodels/torch/mapie are absent as assumed; feasibility failures are compute and memory, not imports.

Keep seven, merged into five lines of work, about 1-1.5 CPU-hours per timeframe in total: (1) one validation harness = quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's SPA, adversarial drift and 5m null tapes folded in (one ledger, one bootstrap, one PBO, active sessions only, every comparator re-priced on the L1 15:25 label); (2) one feature-vocabulary pass = quant-ml-canon-feature-importance, its 8-cluster shortlist frozen in the ledger before any gate search, with BOCPD, FFD and the novelty scalars entering there and nowhere else; (3) one learned-gate family = quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate and decision-making-1 merged (L1 label, capped |net| weights, top-1%-winners-removed as a hard pass, block-wise sign test, one distilled rule list or scorecard as the single OOS candidate from the family); (4) the interpretable candidate = deep-sequence-llm-hypotheses with a blind round 0 from the user's words alone, hashed before any table is shown, and cross-fitted round-1 tables; (5) the cheap desk rule = decision-making-6 session stop with an hour-conditioned null. That yields at most three OOS looks: the rule list from (3), the round-0 list from (4), and the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as comparator, with (5) as a multiplication if its null is rejected.

Drop or defer eleven. The sequence and representation studies (rocket, pretrain, HMM/jump, motif/shapelet, vision) share one structural flaw: the only shippable form is a depth-3 tree on the same scalar features the tabular studies already search, so they add trials to the ledger without adding a candidate, and the pre-SETUP window is templated by the engine's own SETUP definition; pretrain and 1m FQI also need 750-900 MB for hours on a box shared with another build. The two conformal studies and the two sizing studies do not change which SETUPs are taken: they choose a threshold on a score another study produces, or size a positive edge that does not yet exist; their useful pieces (slippage 3/5/8 sensitivity, Pareto front with user-chosen w, |net|-weighted coverage, one-lot-or-skip verdict) become sections of the gate study's deliverable. The regime-breaks study keeps only its break tests as the harness's pre-registration step (they decide time-decay weights and the OOS caveat); BSADF is a feature candidate for the importance pass, not a gate. The exit study is worth its parametric learner C (config keys the lab already has, 10 minutes by replay) but must be coordinated with the ST9-12 session, which already ran an exit grid on 2026.

Two standing caveats every OOS table must carry: the OOS window (2026-01-01..09-25) is also the published lab dashboard window and was used by the ST9-12 exit grid, so it is not pristine; and the 5m Foundation label as built holds 358 of 1,012 trades past the entry session, so ST13/ST14 (square_off 15:25) must be judged on the recomputed intraday label and every comparator re-priced on it.

### Judge 2

Twelve of eighteen studies are worth running here; six are cut or folded. The binding facts: (1) sample size, not compute, is the limit: 684 IS winners on 1m and 184 on 5m, a 15-22% win rate, mean net -922 INR per trade against ~1,050 INR costs, so a gate must find a subset averaging > 16 pts, and the top-decile winners are half of gross wins; every learned number must therefore be reported as a CPCV path distribution (5th percentile), with |net| weights winsorised and kept-n floors. (2) memory: lab.py holds 1.24 GB and 759 MB is free, so the '2 processes under 1 GB' budget is currently one process under ~600 MB; the rocket probe at 10k kernels, the pretrain ladder, 1m FQI and 1m synthetic tapes do not fit until lab.py exits. (3) libraries: everything named that is present imports (numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn 1.7.2 with interaction_cst/monotonic_cst, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, pyarrow, matplotlib, PIL, joblib); statsmodels, torch, mapie, hmmlearn, ruptures, arch are absent and every study that names them correctly hand-codes. Structural fixes that apply across the set: there must be ONE harness (merge quant-ml-canon-purged-cpcv-pbo with decision-making-3's bootstrap/PBO): 12 contiguous IS session blocks, purge by the label's own exit bar, 3-session embargo, one append-only ledger reached only through a score() function, PBO <= 0.2, kept-share/kept-n floors, slippage-8-pt survival, and ONE OOS script run once for at most 3 frozen candidates; all eighteen 'OOS once' clauses collapse into that, otherwise OOS is opened eighteen times. Four near-duplicate pairs merge: meta-label + policy-tree gate (the central study, EV 4), conformal-skip + conformal-risk-control (one operating-point step the user chooses on), the two sizing studies (conditional on a gate surviving; prior is 'one lot or skip'), the two harnesses. The L1 intraday (15:25) label written once is the only training label; the engine label's multi-session holds (358 of 1,012 on 5m) make purging by it too costly. Regime, novelty and state-model outputs enter as candidate features into the importance study rather than as separate gate searches, which is the cheapest cut in multiplicity. The LLM-hypothesis study needs a blind round 0 and a trials count equal to the labelled cells shown; the vision study runs as a 40-session pilot against mechanical proxies first; both must be separate agents from any study author. Cut: pretrain-probe (3-4 h, 750 MB, negative result foreseen), motif/shapelet (keep only the causal novelty score), rocket as proposed (reduce to a 5-minute ceiling check), both sizing studies as standalone. Run order: break tests and L1 label, harness, importance, merged gate, operating point, exit learners C and B (FQI on 5m only), session-stop, BOCPD/GMM regime, LLM rounds, vision pilot, null tapes on 5m; everything above 600 MB waits for lab.py.

## Designers' rationales

- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.
-----
### quant-ml-canon-feature-importance (priority 3)

**technique.** Clustered feature importance (MDA and MDI on correlation clusters, single-feature importance per cluster) under purged cross-validation, the orthogonal-feature sanity check, fractional differentiation (fixed-width FFD with a hand-coded ADF choice of d*) as a candidate feature family, and TreeSHAP interaction values for discovering the 2-3-feature interactions that justify depth-2/3 rules.

**what_it_answers.** Which of the 143 as-of columns (97 numeric, 114 pairs with |rho| > 0.9, so raw importances would be split by substitution) carry information about the intraday Foundation outcome; which at most 8 feature clusters the ST13/ST14 keys should be built from and what their config-expressible representative is; whether the canon's fractionally differentiated price features add anything beyond the ATR-normalised distances already in the table; which feature pairs interact strongly enough to justify a depth-2/3 rule, so that H5's rule search can be restricted (fewer trials, lower PBO).

**method.** (1) Feature set: as-of numeric plus encoded categoricals as in the meta-label study; NaN kept for HGB, a missing-indicator plus median for bagging; columns with > 40% NaN dropped and listed. (2) FFD family: on log close per timeframe, fixed-width fractional differentiation for d in {0.1, 0.2, ..., 1.0} with weight cut 1e-4 (window length recorded); ADF regression with constant and 2 lags hand-coded in numpy (MacKinnon 5% critical value -2.86 embedded and cited); d* = smallest d whose ADF statistic on IS bars is below the critical value; features at the SETUP bar: ffd_close_d*, its z-score against a 60-bar rolling std, the same on log volume; plus the CUSUM-filter counts from the regime study when available. (3) Clustering: Spearman correlation on IS, distance sqrt(0.5 (1 - rho)), scipy average linkage, cut chosen by silhouette in the 20-40 cluster range; every cluster gets a representative chosen by config-expressibility (integer counts and card fields before ATR ratios before raw points). (4) Model and protocol: BaggingClassifier of depth-limited trees on the L1 label with |net| weights under the harness splitter (12 purged, embargoed blocks). Clustered MDA: permute all features of a cluster jointly on the test fold, 5 permutations x 12 folds, record the drop in OOF weighted log-loss and, separately, the drop in OOF kept-vs-skipped expectancy at the fold's tau (the metric that matters); report mean and std across folds; a cluster is kept only when its mean MDA exceeds one std. MDI from the same forest summed per cluster; SFI: each cluster alone under the same CV. (5) Orthogonal check: PCA on standardised IS features, weighted Kendall tau between MDI rank and eigenvalue rank; a low tau is reported as a warning that the importance may be noise-fitting. (6) Interactions: xgboost max_depth 3, 200 rounds, eta 0.05 on the same folds restricted to the top-40 features; shap.TreeExplainer(...).shap_interaction_values on OOF rows; pairs ranked by mean |interaction|; the top 5 pairs with their split points from the tree structure become candidate depth-2/3 rules for H5 and the distillation step. (7) Stability: repeat (4) per IS year (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) and report the rank correlation of cluster importances across years; a feature whose importance is not stable across years is not proposed as a key. Output: importance tables per timeframe, the shortlist (<= 8 clusters with representatives and definitions cited by README name), the FFD verdict, the interaction pairs.

**leakage_controls.** As-of allowlist only (no fwd_*, fnd_*, fzpos_*, fzpost_*, final-state columns); fixed-width FFD is causal by construction and d* is chosen on IS bars only; clustering uses feature values only and is fitted on IS; MDA and SFI are computed on OOF predictions under purging and embargo (permutation on the test fold, model trained on the purged training folds); PCA fitted on IS; nothing is read from OOS; every model fit is logged in the harness ledger although this study proposes no gate itself.

**compute.** FFD over 445k 1m bars x 10 d values with windows up to about 1,000 weights via numpy convolution: 1-2 minutes; ADF: 10 small regressions; clustering on 97 x 97: instant; MDA: 12 fits of a 300-tree bagging on <= 5k rows plus about 40 clusters x 5 permutations x 12 folds = 2,400 predict calls on <= 500 test rows: 5-8 minutes; xgboost and SHAP interactions on <= 5k rows x 40 features, depth 3: about 1 minute, interaction tensor 5k x 40 x 40 float64 = 64 MB (the full 100-feature tensor would be 400 MB, hence the top-40 restriction); total about 15 CPU-minutes per timeframe, peak under 500 MB.

**libraries.** numpy, pandas, scipy (cluster.hierarchy linkage, stats.spearmanr, stats.weightedtau), sklearn (BaggingClassifier, DecisionTreeClassifier, PCA, HistGradientBoostingClassifier, metrics.silhouette_score), xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1; ADF and FFD hand-coded (statsmodels absent).

**output_as_config.** A "features" object in the ST13/ST14 provenance: the ordered shortlist of at most 8 feature names with their README definitions, cluster membership and the per-year stability score; if FFD earns a cluster: {"ffd_d": d*, "ffd_window_bars": w, "ffd_weight_cut": 1e-4, "ffd_z_window": 60} as keys with source "learned:quant-ml-canon-feature-importance", otherwise the recorded verdict "FFD not adopted (clustered MDA <= 1 std)". Thresholds themselves come from the meta-label, sizing and H5 studies, not from here; this study fixes the vocabulary they may use.

**novelty.** AFML (2018) ch. 5 (fractional differentiation, fixed-width FFD, the ADF-minimal d), ch. 8 (MDI, MDA, SFI, orthogonal features and the PCA-rank check); Lopez de Prado, Machine Learning for Asset Managers (2020) ch. 6 (clustered feature importance, the fix for substitution effects that the 2018 chapter did not have); Lundberg et al. (2020) TreeSHAP local explanations and interaction values, Nature Machine Intelligence. Current because clustered MDA plus SHAP interactions is the 2020s replacement for raw MDI rankings, and because it is the only principled way to shrink 143 columns to the 8 the lab's config format allows.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: Trap: clustered MDA on 184 winners (5m) under 12 folds has fold std larger than the mean for nearly every cluster, |net| weighting makes 'important' mean 'recognises the top-decile winners', and FFD of 1-minute log price is a momentum proxy with no prior on this horizon. Fix: run on the binary L1 label with capped weights; make the per-year stability a hard filter (a cluster must rank top-8 in at least 3 of 4 IS years); cap the shortlist at 8 clusters, freeze it in the ledger before any gate study starts so studies 2/7/13 draw features only from it (the single biggest PBO reducer available); FFD, BOCPD run length and the novelty scalars enter here as candidates and nowhere else.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: On 5m replace per-year stability (46 winners per year = noise) with two halves (2021-10..2023-09 vs 2023-10..2025-12) and say so. FFD adoption needs a per-bar FFD routine in fz code, which is a new key type: record it as a user decision, and adopt only if clustered MDA > 1 std on BOTH timeframes. Take the BSADF/CUSUM/BOCPD/novelty scalars from the regime and motif studies as candidate features here rather than letting those studies run their own gate searches (one vocabulary, one ledger). Keep the SHAP interaction step restricted to the top-40 (64 MB tensor) and hand the top-5 pairs to H5 and the distillation step as the only allowed depth-2/3 conjunctions, which is the cheapest PBO reduction in the whole set. Compute ~15 min, < 500 MB: runs now.

### quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip (priority 4)

**technique.** Class-conditional (Mondrian) cross-conformal prediction on the meta-model's nonconformity score, with the skip decision defined as 'win is not in the prediction set', a Mondrian taxonomy by class x time bin for the user's 'different for different time', and Adaptive Conformal Inference for drift in the live/walk-forward version.

#!/bin/bash
# The real run. One thread per fit (bag_probe.log / xgb_probe.log: on the shared 4-core box a 1-thread fit is faster than a
# 4-thread one; the fitted trees are identical either way, random_state fixes them). The stages of one timeframe are independent
# processes (per-stage seeds), so they run in parallel; finalize merges them; shortlist.py freezes the vocabulary.
# In the 2026-09-29 run the 5minute timeframe ran as one `--stage all` process (started before the split) and minute as the
# three parallel stages below; the numbers do not depend on the split.
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
export IMP_BAG_JOBS=1 IMP_XGB_JOBS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
for tf in 5minute minute; do
  for st in main sfi cpcv; do
    nohup python run_importance.py --tf $tf --stage $st > run_${tf}_${st}.nohup 2>&1 &
  done
done
wait
for tf in 5minute minute; do python run_importance.py --tf $tf --stage finalize > run_${tf}_finalize.nohup 2>&1; done
python shortlist.py > shortlist.log 2>&1
echo "run_all done $(date -Is)" >> shortlist.log

"""Repair audit (repair round of 2026-09-29, after the adversarial refuters): the facts behind the 'Repair' section of FINDINGS.md,
computed from the ledger, the registrations, the dry-run logs and the saved fold tables. python repair_audit.py
  -> repair_audit.json, and appends (never edits) one 'correction' record per shortlist registration to ledger/registrations.jsonl
     (idempotent: skipped when a correction for that sha already exists). Read-only on every other file: no model is fitted, no
     OOS row is read, no ledger trial row is written, the shortlist files are only hashed.

Issue 1  the registration note 'frozen before any gate search' is false as a data-ordering fact: the ledger rows before the
         registration are counted per family with first / last timestamps; the phase-3 gate studies (the ones the shortlist
         restricts) are checked for rows; the true ordering goes into the correction record.
Issue 2  the kept-vs-skipped MDA at the fold's tau is undefined wherever the fold's OOF gate skipped nothing: the folds with a
         defined difference are counted from the saved fold tables, the clusters with a defined mean / std from the CSVs.
Issue 3  the dry runs printed real 5minute kept-vs-skipped numbers off-ledger: every configuration-level and fold-level number in
         the four dry logs is inventoried (distinct configurations, evaluations, identical-by-seed check).
Issue 4  the exact-zero contradiction is handled in mda_diag.py (float32-consistent comparison); its json is summarised here."""
import os, re, json, hashlib, datetime as D, collections
import pandas as pd

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)); OUT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
LEDGER = os.path.join(OUT, "ledger")
PHASE3 = ("gate_family", "operating_point_sizing", "llm_round1", "regime_gate", "online_learner")   # PROGRESS.md 'Next' step 1
GATE_SEARCH = ("h2", "h3", "h4", "session_stop", "llm_hypotheses", "rocket", "exit_policy")          # searches for a NEW skip rule
OTHER = {"comparator": "the frozen ST7/ST8 comparator", "h1": "the H1 audit of the frozen gate's own components (not a new rule)",
         "null_tapes_drift": "the real-tape reference rows of the null-tape study", "importance": "this study's own OOF gates (ceilings)"}
DRY_LOGS = ["dry_5minute_attempt1.nohup", "dry_5minute.nohup", "dry_stage_main.nohup", "dry_stage_sfi.nohup"]
sha256 = lambda p: hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- registrations

recomputed drop of ~1e-9 instead of 0 and the exact-zero test `(ll_drop == 0).all()` never fired: the json said 0 exactly-zero

are rounded to float32 before every comparison (like-for-like), so the never-split clusters recompute to exactly 0 in log-loss
and in AUC; (b) 'exactly zero' is also tested by prediction identity (p_perm == float32(p_oof) on every IS row and permutation),
which is the definition ('permuting changes nothing'); (c) the per-period ranks of the stability step are recomputed two ways,
as run (imp_lib.period_mda: float64 base vs float32 permuted) and float32-consistent, and compared: the rounding noise is one

                         auc_mda_pass_mean_gt_std=bool(m > s), auc_mda_folds_positive=int((auc_drop[:, ci] > 0).sum()),
                         auc_mda_pooled=round(float(pooled_drop[ci]), 5)))

        v_run = np.array([np.mean([L.wlogloss(y[rws], pp[ci, r, rws].astype(float), wr) for r in range(L.N_PERM)]) - b64 for ci in range(K)])

                                  noise_is_one_constant=(bool(len(np.unique(np.round(v_run[ident], 15))) == 1) if ident.any() else None),
                                  min_abs_mda_of_split_clusters=(float(np.min(np.abs(v_con[nz]))) if nz.any() else None),
                                  n_clusters_rank_differs=int((r_run != r_con).sum()), rank_as_run_matches_table=bool((r_run == r_tab).all()))
    stab_run = top8_run >= L.STAB_MIN_PERIODS[tf]; stab_con = top8_con >= L.STAB_MIN_PERIODS[tf]

    prc["clusters_stab_changed"] = [dict(cluster=int(c), stab_as_run=bool(stab_run[c]), stab_consistent=bool(stab_con[c]), never_split=bool(ident[c]),
                                         mda_ll_pass=bool(clus_tab.loc[c, "mda_ll_pass"])) for c in np.flatnonzero(stab_run != stab_con)]
    prc["stab_as_run_matches_table"] = bool((stab_run == clus_tab["stab_pass"].to_numpy()).all())
    prc["eligible_consistent"] = int((clus_tab["mda_ll_pass"].to_numpy() & stab_con).sum())

    const_ll = L.wlogloss(y[is_idx], np.full(len(is_idx), pbar_w), wi)

                   float32_precision_note="p_perm is float32; the base p_oof is rounded to float32 before every comparison here (like-for-like); the main stage computed its table in float64 before storage",
                   pooled_oof_auc=round(pooled_base, 4), fold_auc=[round(float(a), 4) for a in base_auc],
                   fold_auc_mean=round(float(base_auc.mean()), 4), fold_auc_std=round(float(base_auc.std(ddof=1)), 4),
                   mean_oof_probability=round(float(p[is_idx].mean()), 4), winner_share=round(pbar, 4), winner_share_net_weighted=round(pbar_w, 4),
                   wlogloss_constant_at_weighted_share=round(const_ll, 5), wlogloss_model_oof=round(model_ll, 5),
                   model_beats_constant_in_wlogloss=bool(model_ll < const_ll),
                   n_clusters_auc_pass=int(tab.auc_mda_pass_mean_gt_std.sum()), n_clusters_ll_negative=int((ll_mean < 0).sum()), n_clusters_ll_positive=int((ll_mean > 0).sum()),
                   n_clusters_ll_zero=int(zero_exact.sum()), n_clusters_ll_zero_by_identity=int(ident.sum()),
                   text_claim_exactly_zero_from_table=n_zero_table, zero_counts_agree=bool(n_zero_table is None or n_zero_table == int(zero_exact.sum())),
                   never_split_clusters=[int(c) for c in np.flatnonzero(ident)],
                   float64_base_noise_max_abs=float(np.max(np.abs(ll_mean64[ident] - ll_mean[ident]))) if ident.any() else 0.0,
                   period_rank_check=prc,
                   top5_by_auc_mda=tab.head(5)[["cluster", "auc_mda_mean", "auc_mda_std", "auc_mda_ratio", "auc_mda_folds_positive", "auc_mda_pooled"]].to_dict(orient="records"))
    print(tf, json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out[tf].items() if k not in ("fold_auc", "top5_by_auc_mda", "period_rank_check", "never_split_clusters")}))
    print(tf, "period_rank_check", json.dumps(prc))
    print(tab.head(8).to_string())
json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(HERE, "mda_diag.json"), "w"), indent=1, default=lambda z: z.item() if hasattr(z, "item") else str(z))

    tab.to_csv(os.path.join(HERE, f"mda_diag_{tf}.csv"), index=False)
    # (c) the per-period ranks of the stability step, as run vs float32-consistent
    per = np.array([L.PERIODS[tf](d) for d in T.day]); pnames = sorted(set(per[is_idx]))
    prc = dict(periods={}, rank_as_run_matches_table=True, clusters_rank_changed=[], clusters_rank_changed_never_split=None, clusters_stab_changed=[],
               eligible_as_run=int((clus_tab["mda_ll_pass"] & clus_tab["stab_pass"]).sum()), eligible_consistent=None, mda_ll_pass_any=bool(clus_tab["mda_ll_pass"].any()))
    top8_run = np.zeros(K, dtype=int); top8_con = np.zeros(K, dtype=int)
    for pn in pnames:
        rws = is_idx[per[is_idx] == pn]; wr = w[rws]
        b64 = L.wlogloss(y[rws], p[rws], wr); b32 = L.wlogloss(y[rws], p32[rws], wr)
        v_run = np.array([np.mean([L.wlogloss(y[rws], pp[ci, r, rws].astype(float), wr) for r in range(L.N_PERM)]) - b64 for ci in range(K)])
        v_con = v_run - b32 + b64
        v_con[ident] = 0.0                                                   # exactly what a float32-consistent period_mda computes
        r_run = (-v_run).argsort().argsort() + 1; r_con = (-v_con).argsort().argsort() + 1
        r_tab = clus_tab[f"rank_{pn}"].to_numpy()
        prc["rank_as_run_matches_table"] &= bool((r_run == r_tab).all())
        top8_run += (r_run <= L.TOP_K_STAB); top8_con += (r_con <= L.TOP_K_STAB)
        nz = ~ident & (v_con != 0)
        prc["periods"][pn] = dict(n_rows=int(len(rws)), noise_constant_never_split=(float(np.unique(np.round(v_run[ident], 15))[0]) if ident.any() else None),
                                  noise_is_one_constant=(bool(len(np.unique(np.round(v_run[ident], 15))) == 1) if ident.any() else None),
                                  min_abs_mda_of_split_clusters=(float(np.min(np.abs(v_con[nz]))) if nz.any() else None),
                                  n_clusters_rank_differs=int((r_run != r_con).sum()), rank_as_run_matches_table=bool((r_run == r_tab).all()))
    stab_run = top8_run >= L.STAB_MIN_PERIODS[tf]; stab_con = top8_con >= L.STAB_MIN_PERIODS[tf]
    ch = np.flatnonzero(top8_run != top8_con)
    prc["clusters_rank_changed"] = [int(c) for c in ch]; prc["clusters_rank_changed_never_split"] = bool(ident[ch].all()) if len(ch) else True
    prc["clusters_stab_changed"] = [dict(cluster=int(c), stab_as_run=bool(stab_run[c]), stab_consistent=bool(stab_con[c]), never_split=bool(ident[c]),
                                         mda_ll_pass=bool(clus_tab.loc[c, "mda_ll_pass"])) for c in np.flatnonzero(stab_run != stab_con)]
    prc["stab_as_run_matches_table"] = bool((stab_run == clus_tab["stab_pass"].to_numpy()).all())
    prc["eligible_consistent"] = int((clus_tab["mda_ll_pass"].to_numpy() & stab_con).sum())
    wi = w[is_idx]
    pbar_w = float((wi * y[is_idx]).sum() / wi.sum()); pbar = float(y[is_idx].mean())
    const_ll = L.wlogloss(y[is_idx], np.full(len(is_idx), pbar_w), wi)
    model_ll = L.wlogloss(y[is_idx], p[is_idx], wi)
    n_zero_table = int(((mda_tab["mda_ll_mean"] == 0) & (mda_tab["mda_ll_folds_positive"] == 0)).sum()) if "mda_ll_folds_positive" in mda_tab else None
    out[tf] = dict(n_is=int(len(is_idx)), n_clusters=K, ll_mda_check_max_abs_diff=check, ll_mda_check_pass=bool(check < 1e-6),
                   ll_mda_check_float64_base_max_abs_diff=check64,
                   float32_precision_note="p_perm is float32; the base p_oof is rounded to float32 before every comparison here (like-for-like); the main stage computed its table in float64 before storage",
                   pooled_oof_auc=round(pooled_base, 4), fold_auc=[round(float(a), 4) for a in base_auc],
                   fold_auc_mean=round(float(base_auc.mean()), 4), fold_auc_std=round(float(base_auc.std(ddof=1)), 4),
                   mean_oof_probability=round(float(p[is_idx].mean()), 4), winner_share=round(pbar, 4), winner_share_net_weighted=round(pbar_w, 4),
                   wlogloss_constant_at_weighted_share=round(const_ll, 5), wlogloss_model_oof=round(model_ll, 5),
                   model_beats_constant_in_wlogloss=bool(model_ll < const_ll),
                   n_clusters_auc_pass=int(tab.auc_mda_pass_mean_gt_std.sum()), n_clusters_ll_negative=int((ll_mean < 0).sum()), n_clusters_ll_positive=int((ll_mean > 0).sum()),
                   n_clusters_ll_zero=int(zero_exact.sum()), n_clusters_ll_zero_by_identity=int(ident.sum()),
                   text_claim_exactly_zero_from_table=n_zero_table, zero_counts_agree=bool(n_zero_table is None or n_zero_table == int(zero_exact.sum())),
                   never_split_clusters=[int(c) for c in np.flatnonzero(ident)],
                   float64_base_noise_max_abs=float(np.max(np.abs(ll_mean64[ident] - ll_mean[ident]))) if ident.any() else 0.0,
                   period_rank_check=prc,
                   top5_by_auc_mda=tab.head(5)[["cluster", "auc_mda_mean", "auc_mda_std", "auc_mda_ratio", "auc_mda_folds_positive", "auc_mda_pooled"]].to_dict(orient="records"))
    print(tf, json.dumps({k: v for k, v in out[tf].items() if k not in ("fold_auc", "top5_by_auc_mda", "period_rank_check", "never_split_clusters")}))
    print(tf, "period_rank_check", json.dumps(prc))
    print(tab.head(8).to_string())

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
